search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Legionnaires' disease cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and outbreak details in New York City during August 2025 (2025-08-01 to 2025-08-31), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, date reported, locality, and evidence quotes.
search_reasoning: The upstream plan contains 10 queries across 5 source-type channels but uses overly rigid quoted phrase constructions (e.g., "Legionnaires disease New York City 2025" as a single quoted phrase) that are unlikely to match real-world document titles or body text precisely, and embeds the date range string "2025-08-01-2025-08-31" literally, which will not match natural-language documents. The upstream queries also duplicate effort across channels with near-identical phrasing. Given the bounds of max 4 queries per iteration and max 10 total, this first iteration must be highly targeted and cover the four most productive channels: (1) NYC DOHMH official public health agency — the primary authoritative source for NYC Legionnaires' disease surveillance and outbreak alerts; (2) NYC Open Data / structured surveillance datasets — NYC publishes Legionnaires' disease case data as open datasets; (3) news search — for August 2025 outbreak reports, case counts, and deaths cited from official sources; (4) CDC/ProMED/WHO international surveillance — for any federal or international situation reports referencing NYC. Queries are rewritten to use natural search syntax rather than over-quoted phrases, and time terms are expressed as natural language ("August 2025") to match how documents are actually written. The NYC DOHMH Health Alert Network (HAN) and Epi Data Brief channels are specifically relevant for Legionnaires' disease, which is a notifiable disease in NYC with periodic outbreak investigations. Cooling tower regulations (Local Law 77) make NYC a high-reporting jurisdiction. ProMED and CDC MMWR are secondary validation sources.

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease New York City August 2025 cases deaths outbreak DOHMH
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) official communications — health alerts, epi data briefs, press releases, and outbreak investigation reports — for Legionnaires' disease in August 2025. DOHMH is the primary authoritative source for NYC Legionnaires' disease surveillance. Natural-language query without over-quoted phrases improves recall against real document text. 'August 2025' matches how documents are dated.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: NYC DOHMH health alert, epi data brief, press release, or outbreak investigation report with case counts and dates
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official NYC government domain (nyc.gov), DOHMH authorship, notifiable disease report language

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease NYC outbreak August 2025 cooling tower cases hospitalizations
query_batch.query_rationale: News sources frequently report NYC Legionnaires' disease outbreaks with case counts, deaths, and borough-level locality details, often citing DOHMH directly. Cooling tower is included because NYC Local Law 77 makes cooling-tower-linked clusters the dominant outbreak type reported in news. August is peak Legionnaires' season (summer), increasing likelihood of news coverage. This query targets news articles from August 2025 that would contain evidence quotes and numerical case data.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News article from major outlet (NYT, NY Post, NY Daily News, Gothamist, AP) reporting case counts, deaths, or outbreak cluster with DOHMH attribution
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Named journalist, DOHMH spokesperson quote, specific case/death numbers, borough or neighborhood location

query_batch.query_rationale: NYC publishes Legionnaires' disease case data through NYC Open Data and DOHMH surveillance datasets. 'Legionella pneumophila' is the scientific term used in dataset field names and metadata. query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: NYC Open Data dataset, DOHMH surveillance summary table, or CDC NNDSS data extract with NYC Legionnaires' case counts for 2025
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official data portal domain (data.cityofnewyork.us, cdc.gov/nndss), dataset metadata with update date, column headers matching case/death fields

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease New York 2025 ProMED MMWR CDC outbreak report August
query_batch.query_rationale: ProMED (Program for Monitoring Emerging Diseases) and CDC MMWR are authoritative secondary validation sources that aggregate and republish outbreak reports, including NYC Legionnaires' disease clusters. ProMED posts are frequently the first internationally visible record of US outbreak investigations. MMWR may publish rapid reports or notes on significant NYC clusters. This query targets these channels specifically for August 2025 NYC events, providing cross-validation of case counts from official NYC sources.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: ProMED archive post with moderator commentary, MMWR citation with DOI, CDC.gov domain, WHO event page

language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. New York City is an English-language jurisdiction; NYC DOHMH publishes all official disease surveillance reports, health alerts, and press releases in English. No localization to other languages is required for this task. Disease terminology is consistent in English: 'Legionnaires' disease', 'Legionellosis', and 'Legionella' are all used in official NYC documents and should be represented across queries to maximize recall.
trust_considerations: Prioritize NYC DOHMH as the primary authoritative source; all other sources should be cross-validated against DOHMH data
News articles are useful for evidence quotes and locality details but case counts must be traced back to official DOHMH attribution
NYC Open Data datasets may have publication lag; verify dataset update date covers August 2025
ProMED posts are secondary aggregators — treat as corroborating, not primary, evidence
Avoid over-reliance on quoted exact-phrase searches that may miss documents using variant terminology (e.g., 'Legionellosis', 'Legionella pneumonia', 'cooling tower illness')
August is peak Legionnaires' season in NYC; expect higher-than-baseline case volumes and potential cluster investigations
NYC Local Law 77 (cooling tower registration and maintenance) means outbreak reports often include cooling tower source identification — this is a trust signal for NYC-specific reports
stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is insufficient on its own; a second iteration will be needed to follow up on any specific outbreak clusters, borough-level breakdowns, or NYC DOHMH data portal datasets identified in iteration 1 results. Stop after iteration 2 if core case/death counts and at least one official source URL are identified.
warnings: Upstream queries used over-quoted exact phrases (e.g., '"Legionnaires disease New York City 2025"') and literal date-range strings ('2025-08-01-2025-08-31') that are unlikely to match real document text — these have been rewritten with natural-language phrasing
The time window (August 2025) is recent; some official surveillance reports or datasets may not yet be published or may have publication lag of 4–8 weeks

Peer-reviewed literature (upstream q_exec_005/006) is deprioritized in iteration 1 because academic publications on a specific August 2025 event are extremely unlikely to exist within weeks of the event — this channel is deferred to iteration 2 if needed
Max 4 queries per iteration enforced; the 10 upstream queries have been consolidated into 4 high-priority, non-redundant queries covering the most productive channels
If no August 2025 specific outbreak is found, iteration 2 should broaden to NYC DOHMH annual surveillance summaries or NYC Open Data Legionnaires' dataset filtered to 2025

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong, highly relevant evidence confirming a major Legionnaires' disease outbreak in Central Harlem, NYC during August 2025. Key quantitative signals are already visible in snippets: 67 cases / 3 deaths (Aug 5), 101 cases / 4 deaths (Aug 14), 112–113 cases / 6 deaths (Aug 25–26), 104+ cases / 7 deaths (Aug 29–30), and 90 hospitalizations (Guardian, Aug 30). The outbreak was declared over on Aug 29. However, three important gaps remain: (1) The nyc.gov domain returned 4 results but the snippets only show the Aug 14 press release — additional official NYC DOHMH press releases (early-outbreak Aug 5 release, Aug 18 update, Aug 26/27 update, and the Aug 29 outbreak-over declaration) are likely on nyc.gov and should be surfaced to anchor authoritative source URLs; (2) CDC.gov returned 3 results but no snippet content was shown — CDC MMWR or NNDSS data for this outbreak may provide structured case/death counts and should be confirmed; (3) The Bronx isolated cases mentioned in the respiratory-therapy.com snippet (two cases in a condominium) represent a secondary cluster that may have separate case counts not yet captured. A second iteration with 4 targeted queries can close these gaps efficiently within the 10-query budget (4 used + 4 new = 8 total, within limit).
